source.title: Non-vacuous Generalization Bounds at the ImageNet Scale: a PAC-Bayesian Compression Approach
source.authors: Wenda Zhou; Victor Veitch; Morgane Austern; Ryan P. Adams; Peter Orbanz

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present, including appendices.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports its own CIFAR-10 label-randomization experiment and measures how compression after training relates to training accuracy as randomization increases. This bears on V1's distinction between natural-label generalization and random-label memorization, but it does not directly report held-out accuracy for those conditions.
record.gate_note: The paper's compression bounds and examples are results about bounds, not direct measurements of the claim versions. The CIFAR-10 randomization experiment reports training accuracy after pruning at different target sparsities; those results are included because the study applies label randomization and measures the resulting model behavior. The paper also cites Zhang et al. (2017a), but those cited results are not extracted as rows.
record.test_reason: Section 6 repeats the label-randomization test and reports that its ResNet-56 reaches 100% training accuracy at every randomization level. This tests V1's random-label fitting component, although the study does not report the corresponding held-out accuracies.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially accurate: the authors obtain non-vacuous compression-based generalization bounds and report that greater label randomization reduces compressibility under a fixed scheme. They also emphasize that the bounds remain far from tight.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies PAC-Bayesian bounds based on compression and reports a separate label-randomization/pruning experiment. It does not reproduce the original claim's held-out accuracy comparisons or the other version-specific interventions.
record.method_sensitivity: In the CIFAR-10 compression experiment, faster training-accuracy decay at higher pruning levels is reported for scenarios with more label randomization.

fits_no_version.finding: All randomization conditions tolerate 50% sparsity with essentially unchanged training accuracy; beyond that, training accuracy falls faster with greater label randomization.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: For this architecture and pruning scheme, greater label randomization reduces compressibility at higher sparsities.

record.problems: The label-randomization experiment reports post-pruning training accuracy but no held-out accuracy for the randomized conditions. Figure 1 provides the plotted training-performance result; the text describes the trend but gives no numerical values for the decay.
record.rows_left_out: No other rows meet the requested claim-version measures. Compression-bound values in Section 5 measure bounds rather than the version-specific generalization behaviors, and optimizer and batch-size details in Appendix B are experiment settings, not comparisons.

untested.parts: Held-out accuracy above chance on natural labels and at chance on random labels under the same architecture and training recipe.
Test error as width increases beyond interpolation.
Convolutional versus fully connected image-classification performance and the contribution of locality.
Held-out performance comparisons between adaptive optimizers and SGD under controlled tuning.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Whether magnitude-aware sharpness ranks generalization gaps better than alternative measures; noise robustness is used to construct bounds without testing this comparison.
Test accuracy after removing highly memorized versus randomly selected training examples.

missing.what: Add the pre-pruning training result: ResNet-56 achieves 100% training accuracy at every tested label-randomization level, including completely random labels. The authors report this for their experiment while noting agreement with Zhang et al.; it is not merely a cited result.
missing.locator: Section 6, Experiments, immediately before the paragraph describing pruning; Figure 1.

record.verdict_notes: Missing held-out measurements leave V1's generalization component untested; they do not establish an absent effect or a scope limitation.

versions.untested_parts: The experiment varies label randomization and reports training accuracy after pruning, but does not report held-out accuracy on natural versus random labels.
The paper does not sweep network width or report test error across widths.
The paper does not compare convolutional and fully connected networks on image test error.
The paper does not compare adaptive optimizers with SGD on held-out performance; optimizer mentions in experiment details are not such a comparison.
The paper does not compare batch sizes or report a large-batch generalization gap.
The paper does not test dropout.
The paper does not measure magnitude-aware sharpness or compare it with generalization gaps.
The paper does not remove memorized examples and measure test accuracy.

rows.subject: ResNet with 56 layers
rows.operation_detail: Trained on CIFAR-10 with labels randomized at the stated levels, then compressed by pruning to varying target sparsities; the result reports training accuracy after pruning.
rows.value: All networks achieve 50 % sparsity with essentially no loss of training accuracy, even on completely random labels; as compression increases further, scenarios with more randomization exhibit a faster decay in training accuracy.
rows.note: The described metric is training accuracy after compression, not held-out accuracy, so it cannot establish V1's natural-label versus random-label test-performance contrast.
rows.check: The pruning trend measures compressibility, not V1's coexistence of memorization and generalization. Its baseline is each network's pre-pruning training accuracy, reported as 100% at every randomization level.

relationships.condition: Random-label fitting component only: ResNet-56 on CIFAR-10 without preprocessing or penalization.
relationships.reason: Section 6 explicitly reports 100% training accuracy at every label-randomization level, including 100%; this verdict rests on text missing from the rows, not R1's pruning trend.
relationships.display_finding: The reported perfect training fit across label-randomization levels remains unverified from the available source.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
